topicName: GitLab CI/CD: Runners, Stages, Jobs, and Include Directives
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering GitLab CI/CD: Runners, Stages, Jobs, and Include Directives"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitLab CI/CD is a powerful built-in tool for software development through continuous integration, delivery, and deployment. This tutorial covers the foundational concepts required to build scalable pipelines."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Core Pipeline Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"At the heart of GitLab CI/CD are three main structural components: Jobs, Stages, and Runners. Together, they define what tasks to execute, the order of execution, and the computing environment where they run."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Jobs: The fundamental units of a CI/CD pipeline that define what needs to be done, such as compiling code or running tests."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stages: Logical groupings of jobs. Jobs in the same stage execute in parallel, while stages execute sequentially."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Runners: Lightweight, isolated agents that pick up and execute the jobs defined in your .gitlab-ci.yml file."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Writing Your First Pipeline"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following configuration demonstrates a simple pipeline with three distinct stages: build, test, and deploy."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"stages:
  - build
  - test
  - deploy

compile_code:
  stage: build
  script:
    - echo "Compiling the application..."
    - mkdir build
    - touch build/app.bin
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - build/

run_tests:
  stage: test
  script:
    - echo "Running unit tests..."
    - ./build/app.bin --test

deploy_production:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - echo "Deploying to production server..."
  only:
    - main"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Scaling with Include Directives"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"As projects grow, single-file configurations become difficult to maintain. The 'include' keyword allows you to break down your CI/CD configuration into multiple reusable files, promoting DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principles across repositories."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"include:
  - local: '/ci/templates/docker-build.yml'
  - project: 'devops/ci-templates'
    file: '/security-扫描.yml'
    ref: 'main'

stages:
  - build
  - security
  - deploy"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Configuring GitLab Runners"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Runners can be shared across multiple projects, specific to a single project, or restricted to particular groups. To register a runner locally on your infrastructure, use the following registration command:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"gitlab-runner register \
  --non-interactive \
  --url "https://gitlab.com/" \
  --registration-token "GLRT-1234567890abcdef" \
  --executor "docker" \
  --docker-image "alpine:latest" \
  --description "docker-runner-01""},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"By correctly orchestrating runners, stages, jobs, and include directives, you can establish an enterprise-grade CI/CD pipeline that remains clean, modular, and performant as your codebase scales."}]
